name: Mannat Kaur Randhawa
feedback: The bold game styling and room-based flow are convincing: creating a room, starting a round, and restoring it after reload worked. Tighten judging and timing feedback—the empty round awarded a point—and verify a full multi-player round so scoring feels dependable.
tested: Screenshot; created private room with synthetic name; started game; round advanced to result and next-round control; room restored after reload; empty four-answer result received +1.
limitations: No chat messages or public lobby used; multiplayer and AI judgment quality not verified.

name: Vedanth Bhat
feedback: The restaurant and hotel registries, detailed scoring breakdowns, and working search make the idea easy to explore. The seed-model disclosure is useful, but prominently distinguish every demonstration score and stock image from verified venue evidence before presenting this as service-quality intelligence.
tested: Inspected screenshot; Restaurants, Hotels, Rankings, Compare, Methodology; filtered 25 restaurants to Indian Accent; opened detailed evidence/model page.
limitations: Seed data explicitly disclosed; ingestion and independent evidence verification not demonstrated; persistence not established.

name: Vishal Gupta
feedback: The arcade styling and functioning pause/restart loop give the game a recognizable identity. Clean up the checkerboard image backgrounds and make Settings meaningful; add a clear start screen and explain the scoring and obstacle rules.
tested: Screenshot; live score advanced; Menu paused; RESTART reset score to zero; Settings produced no visible panel.
limitations: Hosted within Stitch preview; movement and collision handling not comprehensively tested; persistence unknown.

name: Dhruv Singhal
feedback: The crisis-response concept is thoughtfully modeled with separate consumer, responder, operations, and audit screens, and unusually clear warnings that this is only a demonstration. The scripted scenario creates a queued incident, but reload returns to the opening state; show a complete durable handoff and recovery path before treating this as usable infrastructure.
tested: Screenshot; all four main surfaces; scripted end-to-end control created INC-2407 with triage and dispatch state; reload returned to demonstration gate/home.
limitations: All responders/providers explicitly mocked; no real calls, messages or permissions used.

name: Divyansh Pugalia
feedback: The mobile emergency dashboard prioritizes help clearly, and the network, medical profile, and full-screen Medical ID form a coherent journey. Replace the fixed profile/GPS presentation and demo bed availability with trustworthy, consent-aware data, and make clear which emergency actions are actually connected.
tested: Screenshot; Help, Network, Me; Medical ID opened/closed; Beds available filter selected.
limitations: SOS, calls and messages intentionally not triggered; seeded records unchanged; contact persistence not tested.

name: Bipasha Das
feedback: The real-or-satire decision followed by a strategic-intent question turns brand trivia into a useful learning activity. Correct answers produced points and a specific explanation, and progress survived reload; strengthen it with source links for campaign claims and richer end-of-game feedback.
tested: Screenshot; completed IKEA truth and strategy questions; earned 100 points and autopsy; advanced to KFC; card 2 and score restored after reload.
limitations: Full ten-card completion and CMO radar not tested; campaign facts not independently verified.

name: Aryan Singh
feedback: The five-step onboarding and founder idea deck present a focused, attractive cofounder-matching concept. The profile shows three matches while navigation shows one, and reload loses the completed onboarding; make those counts consistent and persist the profile before expanding the matching claims.
tested: Screenshot; completed synthetic onboarding; inspected Deck, Matches, Post and Profile; reload reset to first onboarding step.
limitations: Explicit demo build; no public idea posted or messages sent; real matching backend not demonstrated.

name: Prit Jain
feedback: The take-home earnings model is well chosen, with useful cost, waiting-time, platform comparison, and history views; the saved rider preference survived reload. Improve incomplete-input handling—the form displayed ₹5,000/hour before valid times existed—and make the AI analysis resolve reliably instead of leaving the user in an analyzing state.
tested: Screenshot; Home, Add Shift, History, Compare, Insights and Settings; saved synthetic rider name and verified reload; payout updated calculation; form validation prevented invalid save.
limitations: Sample shifts clearly isolated in Demo Mode; valid shift creation not completed because time inputs did not retain entry; AI result not observed.

name: Anushka Mittal
feedback: The Jaipur identity, imagery, artisan stories, and broad catalogue create a strong branded shopping experience. Fix untranslated labels such as brandPromiseDesc and shippingReturns, and persist cart changes—the added item disappeared after reload—before calling the store complete.
tested: Screenshot; Home, Shop, Our Story, Artisans, Explore Jaipur, Sustainability; searched pouch; Add to Cart changed count 2→3; reload restored 2.
limitations: No checkout or purchase; artisan and sustainability claims not independently verified.

name: Kanan Goyal
feedback: The restrained visual identity carries through a coherent assessment, personalized ritual, and usage calendar; the logged ritual survived reload. Add credible sourcing for the precise skin-outcome timelines and make the product/sample boundary explicit so an elegant commerce experience does not imply clinical certainty.
tested: Screenshot; completed four synthetic assessment answers; Ritual, Rhythm, Origin, Log; logged one use and verified persistence after reload.
limitations: No purchase, photo upload or real health data; assessment outputs not validated clinically; sample batch not verified.

name: Medha Raghuvanshi
feedback: The dish-first discovery and saved-bites flow are clear, and guest onboarding plus saved food survived reload. Make profile counts reflect actual activity—the new profile claimed 82 bites and six DineSyncs despite one saved dish—and identify sample offers/history before users rely on them.
tested: Screenshot; guest setup, Save, Saved, DineSync, Explore, Profile; saved pasta persisted across reload.
limitations: Group matching, offer validity and restaurant data not independently verified; no booking, sharing or phone sign-in.

name: Ishaan Jain
feedback: The sign-in screen is tidy and establishes a clear money-management identity. Provide a guest mode or reviewer account so expense entry, totals, and saved records can actually be assessed; the brief was also unavailable through the connected Drive account.
tested: Screenshot and sign-in UI inspected; no guest/demo option; brief connector returned file-not-found.
limitations: Authentication blocks all core functionality; no account created.

name: Jyoti Kumari Singh
feedback: The visual humor, employee badge, scenario choice, and persona reveal hold together well, and the profile survived reload. Finish the promised progression—Level 2 is still Coming Soon—and make the analysis explain how answers produce the percentages rather than just presenting impressive-looking readings.
tested: Screenshot; employee onboarding; scenario answer advanced to 2/10; analysis/persona; reload retained name/persona; Level 2 landing says Coming Soon.
limitations: Skipped remainder via offered analysis shortcut; later levels unavailable; AI/backend scoring not verified.

name: Diksha Matia
feedback: The habit library, learning sections, and local XP tracking give this a useful structure; marking a habit earned 20 XP that survived reload. Reconcile the analytics with real activity—the fresh session already showed 12.4k XP and a brain score of 94—and source or clearly label the cognitive metrics and scientific claims.
tested: Screenshot; all eleven main navigation sections; completed one habit; XP 20/120 persisted after reload; analytics showed unrelated prefilled totals.
limitations: No clinical validity assessed; AI coach response and drill completion not tested; metrics partly demonstrative.

name: Haryashwa Singh Thakore
feedback: The agricultural marketplace has a coherent visual language and usable navigation across mandi, logistics, credit support, and corporate pages. The working crop filter is a good start, but verified KYC, live prices, escrow totals, and dispatch claims need explicit demo labeling and a proven end-to-end transaction path.
tested: Screenshot; all five primary sections; Wheat filter narrowed market to one listing; reload restored overview.
limitations: No bids, loans, bookings or KYC changes submitted; escrow/logistics and price provenance not verified.

name: Esheta Rathi
feedback: The mood-based mini-game choice and timed odd-one-out interaction work cleanly, with visible score and streak feedback. Preserve an active session across reload—the 10-point run returned to Ready—and enforce the advertised hard cap and cooldown even when users refresh; saved profile naming already persists.
tested: Screenshot; mood and length choice; started 5-minute session; correct answer gave 10 points; reload lost active run; Leaders and Profile visited; synthetic profile saved through reload.
limitations: Session completion/cooldown not verified; only first mini-game tested.

name: Vanshica Sharma
feedback: The wardrobe editor has a distinct scrapbook aesthetic and a useful closet-to-outfit-to-lookbook journey. Increase text contrast and persist saved looks—the lookbook rose from two to three, then returned to two after reload—and clearly distinguish sample weather and wear statistics from personal data.
tested: Screenshot; Today, Quiz, Closet, Lookbook; saved outfit raised count 2→3; reload lost it.
limitations: Photo tagging and personalized weather not verified; seeded wardrobe unchanged.

name: Janvi Arora
feedback: The memory game is simple and understandable, with working flips, mismatch recovery, a move counter, timer, and restart. Improve the fit of the board within the screen and the accessible labels—an unmatched revealed card is announced as Matched—and add difficulty or best-score tracking to give the concept more depth.
tested: Screenshot; revealed two different cards; move counter incremented; mismatched pair hid again; timer advanced; Restart reset timer and moves.
limitations: Full-board victory and reload persistence not tested; single-screen game only.

name: Arshia Gupta
feedback: The focused case workflow generated a relevant guesstimate and detailed feedback that directly addressed the submitted assumptions and arithmetic. Preserve completed attempts after reload, and distinguish sourced market facts from illustrative estimates in the consultant answer.
tested: Selected case type and difficulty; Generated case; Submitted synthetic estimate and received tailored rubric feedback; Reload returned to case selection.
limitations: One case tested; accuracy of external market and regulatory claims not verified.

name: Aadi Jain
feedback: The product clearly separates Android automation from the usable browser ledger, and a synthetic expense survived reload while the sample alert parsed the correct merchant and amount. Strengthen confidence with demonstrated import/export and signed-in sync tests, alongside the existing explicit privacy and platform boundaries.
tested: Guest manual expense saved and retained after reload; Overview and Transactions navigation; Sample bank alert parsed as Zomato expense450; Product guide inspected.
limitations: Android installation, permission-based capture, signed-in cloud sync, CSV import/export not exercised.

name: Akash V
feedback: The salon discovery, appointment view, style advisor and partner screens form a coherent and visually polished demo. The booking summary defaulted to yesterday despite showing future date choices, so validate date selection and make the simulated availability, invoices and partner access unmistakable before real use.
tested: Discovery and salon detail; AI style recommendation generated; My Appointments; Partner dashboard, slot schedule and storefront editor; Booking summary inspected without reservation.
limitations: No booking, payment, messages or seeded-record edits; availability and AI venue accuracy unverified.

name: Rishika
feedback: The fragrance store has a consistent premium visual style, and cart additions survived reload while the quiz produced a usable product match. Fix the recommendation content binding: a Kyoto Cypress result displayed an Oceanic Night description, which undermines confidence in the personalization.
tested: Home Shop Cart Quiz navigation; Added Alpine Mist to cart and verified reload retention; Completed three-step scent quiz.
limitations: No checkout or payment; inventory, delivery and recommendation logic beyond one path not verified.

name: Shreya Vermani
feedback: The three reflection prompts produced a personalized title and a playable sequence with a clear cinematic tone. The result claimed to be saved to a weekly season, but reload returned to an empty form with no visible history; make that saved collection accessible and explain what is actually retained.
tested: Three synthetic reflections entered; Trailer generated and played to completion; Rewatch and next-cut controls visible; Reload reset to empty form.
limitations: No photos uploaded; audio quality and weekly finale not verified.

name: Mansa Bihani
feedback: The lobby readiness gate, discovery quiz, voting and two scenario outcomes make a lively and coherent game demo. The lobby promises three scenarios but reaches analytics after two, and reload resets the roster and active game despite cloud-sync language; align the promised session with actual progression and persistence.
tested: Added bot and satisfied readiness gate; Discovery quiz and skip; Voted through two missions; Analytics and profile screens; Reload reset roster and active route.
limitations: No multiplayer invitation, squad messages or external backup; seeded analytics and cloud claims unverified.

name: Manya Mahajan
feedback: A synthetic task was parsed, created and retained after reload, and the main administrative sections are connected. Improve the generated steps: organizing a bookshelf incorrectly required ID and an online application, while the calendar remained anchored to October 2023; low-contrast secondary text also needs attention.
tested: All six main navigation sections; Synthetic task extraction and creation; Reload retained task; Calendar and task detail inspected.
limitations: No real documents, messages or payments; security and compliance claims unverified.

name: Shivang Chaudhary
feedback: The submitted link opens a Google Doc that requires access, and the supporting brief was also unavailable through Drive. Provide a publicly viewable app or a working demo link so the interface and core workflow can be evaluated.
tested: Submitted Google Doc opened and showed access request; Supporting brief fetch returned404.
limitations: No app UI or functionality observable; no access request sent.

name: Vedant Mazumdar
feedback: The music-detective theme carries through a working daily challenge, escalating clues, scored result, archive, statistics and a separate practice room. A wrong guess survived reload and the solved case appeared in the archive; improve visibility of navigation during an active case and document audio sourcing and playback fallback behavior.
tested: Playback control changed state; Wrong guess unlocked more tape; Reload retained wrong guess; Second guess solved daily case with850points; Case File Record Practice navigation.
limitations: Audio fidelity and licensing not verified; no sharing or next-day unlock tested.

name: Adithiyha Kamaraj
feedback: The visual system is consistent across Home, Tasks, Vault, Activity and Circle, but the app currently behaves mainly as a populated interface mock. Add life event and Add family member produced no visible form, and the user changed from Adi to Elena across screens; connect a complete create-edit-save flow and use one consistent demo identity.
tested: All five main navigation screens; Add life event and Circle Add controls; Reload retained route.
limitations: No real uploads, financial actions or messages; sample synced records not verified.

name: Vansh Jindal
feedback: The public landing page clearly explains the career-decision journey and presents a polished visual hierarchy. The analysis entry led to a Google sign-in requirement with no offered demo, so provide a guest walkthrough to make the actual recommendations and saved workflows assessable.
tested: Landing and product links; Analysis entry; Login page inspected.
limitations: Core analysis, application tracking, spend and persistence unavailable without sign-in; no account created.

name: Hindavi Nitin Patil
feedback: The gear guide, contextual FAQ and persistent packing checklist create a useful preparation flow with a clear visual identity. The readiness screen declared preparation complete and verified with only 1 of 19 items packed, so gate that assurance on essential equipment and show missing safety items explicitly.
tested: Home Gear Checklist Chatbot Profile; Packed one item and retained it after reload; Readiness check at5percent; Contextual water FAQ answered.
limitations: No real trek undertaken; safety guidance accuracy not independently verified.

name: Mehak Garg
feedback: The calm visual language, saved local journal and check-in, breathing timer and explicit sample-circle labels fit the wellbeing concept well. Support and My Week both open a page-not-found screen; repair these main routes, especially the urgent-support destination, before relying on this as a campus safe space.
tested: All main navigation routes; Synthetic check-in and journal retained after reload; Breathing timer progressed; Circles sample-content notice; Reflection Buddy and Settings inspected.
limitations: No community post or real personal health data; support route unavailable.

name: Ashu Bhatia
feedback: The five-round draft, animated card reveal and 86-point result form a complete, enjoyable short game with a strong football identity. Preserve the completed team or best score after reload, explain the rating basis, and replace the XI wording with the actual five-player format.
tested: All5draft selections; Revealed5cards; Scores15+17+16+20+18 correctly totaled86; Reload returned to landing.
limitations: No share action; audio quality and rating accuracy unverified.

name: Aman Pundir
feedback: The calorie dashboard and manual meal form are easy to follow, and adding a 123 kcal sample correctly updated the total from 860 to 983. The meal disappeared after reload, and skipping the photo still claimed an estimate from a photo; retain logs and clearly separate sample estimates from genuine analysis.
tested: Dashboard Log Progress Settings; Skipped photo and manually logged synthetic123kcalmeal; Verified immediate calorie total; Reload lost added meal.
limitations: No camera permissions granted or personal health data; photo recognition and predictive claims unverified.

name: Reena Rewri
feedback: The marketplace has an inviting food-led design, working search and useful pickup and availability details. The brownie page says 21 reviews while its review section says 0, and a 23-day-old listing is still presented as freshly posted; reconcile these trust signals and expose a safe demo of the authenticated seller and reservation flow.
tested: Search narrowed to brownie; Food detail inspected; Cravings Sell My Food Me access states.
limitations: Account-required actions, reservations, seller creation and persistence not tested; no booking or messages.

name: Harshit Baid
feedback: The single-screen clock and alarm controls are clear, and saving and clearing the default alarm both survived reload. The demonstrated scope is very small; add an immediate alarm test, clear browser-background limitations and a visible ringing/snooze state so reliability can be assessed.
tested: Live clock; Default7AMalarm save and reload; Clear and reload confirmed no alarm.
limitations: Time-edit automation did not retain chosen value; actual scheduled ringing, sound and background behavior unverified.

name: Rishabh Bhandari
feedback: The interactive cost curves, revenue view and data schedule make the economic model inspectable, and raising price from $17 to $20 correctly increased current profit from $1,000 to $10,000. Include zero output in shutdown optimization: at price $10 it warns to shut down yet labels one unit as the optimal output; also save scenarios and qualify optima limited by the plotted range.
tested: All3analysis tabs; Price17→20 current-profit consistency; Price10shutdown edge case; Reload reset inputs.
limitations: One parameter sweep; CSV export and full optimizer mathematics not exhaustively verified.

name: Aadi Jain
feedback: The product clearly separates Android automation from a usable guest ledger, and a synthetic expense survived reload while the sample alert parsed correctly. Demonstrate signed-in sync and CSV round-trip reliability next, while preserving the clear privacy and platform boundaries.
tested: Independently reviewed alternate deployment of row174 app; Saved123expense and retained after reload; Overview Transactions Alert demo; Sample450Zomatoalert parsed.
limitations: Same app design as174; guide evidence reused from174. Android capture, authenticated sync and CSV round-trip not exercised.

name: Soham Dhamnaskar
feedback: The core triage flow generated relevant urgent, delegated and FYI items from synthetic input, and the brief survived reload. Fix the missing icon font, connect archive metrics to actual generated work, and avoid drafting an unconditional approval when the input merely says approval is needed.
tested: DailyInput Brief Archives Intelligence Settings; Synthetic3itembrief generated; Reload retained latestbrief.
limitations: External integrations, team actions and archive persistence of newbrief unverified; no messages sent.

name: Tanisha
feedback: The site presents styling services, pricing and the matching request clearly with a strong editorial visual style. Replace the placeholder contact number and substantiate the 2,500-plus transformation claim and testimonials; a safe demo of stylist matching and post-booking support would show how much works beyond the landing page.
tested: Service pricing and creator sections; Pro CTA moved to matchingform; Date/occasion request form inspected; Login modal.
limitations: No booking, account, contact submission, calls or messages; authenticated consultation and persistence unverified.

name: Ishani Handa
feedback: The city setup, trip planner and detailed itinerary make the concierge concept tangible, with sample-plan labelling and connected Trips/Profile screens. The ₹20,500-per-person plan has a cost breakdown summing to ₹25,000, so reconcile pricing and clearly distinguish sample availability from real reservations before enabling checkout.
tested: Cityandpreferenceonboarding; Generated3sampleManaliplans; Detailedcostanditinerary; Home Plan Trips Profile; Reloadretainedprofile.
limitations: No reservations, payments, concierge messages or real personal data; provider availability not verified.

name: Aditya Jain
feedback: The landing page clearly separates manager and tenant needs and describes an India-specific rent and utility workflow. Both roles require sign-in and offer no demo access, so the invoice splitting, maintenance board and retained records remain unassessed; provide a sample property with safe demo roles.
tested: Landing inspected; Manager login; Tenant login.
limitations: No account created; authenticated features and persistence unobservable.

name: Kushal Sethia
feedback: The wallet, category recommendation and spending planner work together, with a sample ₹2,000 monthly spend correctly yielding ₹100 in estimated rewards and both wallet and inputs retained after reload. Improve the decision model by surfacing annual fees, caps and exclusions beside net rewards, and add dates and issuer sources to the clearly labelled prototype rules.
tested: All6mainroutes; AddedcatalogSBIcard without credentials; Online2000recommendation and5percentreward; Spending profile; Reload retainedwalletandspend.
limitations: One card and category tested; current issuer terms not validated and no financial transaction.

name: Prakul Bansal
feedback: The terminal has a coherent research layout and explicitly explains its bring-your-own-key model and estimate limitations. Company research correctly stopped at the missing Finnhub key, so provide a fixture-backed demo to let reviewers test analysis, comparisons and saved ideas without handling credentials.
tested: Walkthrough exit; Company research missing-key state; Sector Pulse Compare Watchlist screens.
limitations: No API keys supplied; live data, AI research, scoring and watchlist persistence unobservable.

name: Ananya Chhibba
feedback: The mood-to-three-picks flow gives distinct musical directions and carries the chosen track into an editable story layout. Caption changes reset on reload and playback buttons lead to YouTube searches rather than a resolved track; retain story edits and make the listening handoff more precise.
tested: Home Curate Explore; Studyingprompt to moodanalysis and3picks; Trackdetail and story; Changedcaption; Reloadretainedtrack but resetcaption.
limitations: No photo upload or public sharing; actual music playback and recommendation generation method not verified.

name: Abhay Sharma
feedback: The interactive lunar presentation has a distinct visual identity and the registry search narrows the sample records. The claim flow is only a waitlist, while totals jump from 1,247 on Explore to 14,293 in Registry; carry the illustrative-data disclaimer across all pages and remove unsupported verified-ownership language.
tested: Explore3Dview screenshot; Registry searchTycho reduced5to1; About; Claimwaitlist; Reload.
limitations: No email submission; ownership/legal and live telemetry claims unverified; map drag not exercised.

name: Muskan Garg
feedback: The XP-staked goal concept is engaging, and a private test goal deducted 100 XP and accepted a progress update. Choosing a preset stake erased the draft and reverted Private to Public, and reload lost the newly created goal; preserve form state and privacy choices, then persist goal progress reliably.
tested: All6mainnavigation screens; Privategoal created usingmanualstake input; XP2450→2350; Progressupdate; Preset100button erasedformandprivacy; Reload lostgoal.
limitations: No public goal, social backing or seededgoal edits; completion reward and fulldeadline lifecycle not tested.

name: Satyajit Mohanty
feedback: The two-member trip and expense flow is clear, and a ₹100 expense correctly produced a single ₹50 settlement from the non-payer to the payer. Reload discarded the entire trip, so persistent trip storage and a way to reopen, edit and reconcile past expenses are the next essentials.
tested: Created synthetic trip with2members; Added100expense toTestAlex; Equal50split and settlement verified; Reload returned to landing.
limitations: One expense/two-member case; no payment or sharing; rounding and larger settlement graphs not tested.

name: Saksheth Akshay Rao
feedback: The login screen has a calm, consistent visual design and labels phone and Google sign-in as unavailable. No guest route is offered, so the main Nurture workflow and saved state cannot be assessed; include a safe demonstration account or public walkthrough.
tested: Login screen inspected; Disabled phone and Google sign-in visible.
limitations: No account created; core app and persistence unobservable.

name: Utsav Sharma
feedback: The receivables dashboard and recovery screens are visually organized, but the invoice workflow is still disconnected. A manually entered REVIEW-DEMO-001 for ₹123 became an unrelated ₹4,250 sample invoice with a claim that it was extracted from an upload; preserve the actual input and verify the full draft workflow before exposing irreversible sending or legal-escalation actions.
tested: All6mainroutes; Synthetic manual invoice input; Next step replaced it withsampleinvoice; Recovery and escalation draft inspected without sending; Reload and dashboard.
limitations: No debtor contact data entered, notices sent, payments or upgrades; legal and recovery-probability claims not validated.

name: Amitesh Kumar
feedback: The mood questionnaire produces a relevant new recipe and the presentation is visually coherent. Selecting Vegan still returned two salmon dishes alongside the plant-based result, and a saved recommendation vanished after reload; enforce dietary exclusions across every result and persist the collection before adding stronger matching claims.
tested: Homequestionnaire relaxed/healthy/vegan; Generatedpowerbowl plus2salmonresults; Savedcount4→5; Reloadresetto4; Saved History AIAssistant screens.
